outcome: Hold every Latin-script word of a one-name dataset reference to the not-found rule: a stopword or hint word inside a name that says more than a hint, and a dot suffix that is not the extension of a file a dataset is imported from, must be accounted for like any other word, so references such as orders.backup, orders_latest, data_orders and lib_latest no longer resolve silently to another dataset
criteria: In a workspace whose only dataset is orders, the one-name references orders.west and orders.backup are NOT_FOUND with west and backup in absent_words, while orders.csv, orders.json and orders.parquet still resolve to orders: only a trailing suffix that names a tabular artifact kind (csv, json, parquet, db, sqlite, sqlite3) is set aside as the file a dataset came from

A one-name reference that has a word other than stopwords and hint words holds its Latin-script stopwords and hint words (such as file, data, table, by or latest) to the rule too: orders_file, data_orders and orders_latest are NOT_FOUND naming that word instead of resolving to orders, and lib_latest is NOT_FOUND with the lib_ datasets as nearest names instead of resolving to the newest of them; such a word that a dataset's name, alias, description or columns account for still lets the reference resolve

A reference made only of stopwords and hint words (latest, yesterday), a reference with whitespace, and words in CJK scripts keep today's resolution and scoring; tests in tests/test_resolution.py cover each case above, and README.md and the resolver's module docstring state the rule

dispositions.note: DatasetResolver._score sets aside a trailing dot suffix only when ArtifactKind.for_suffix names a tabular kind. test_a_suffix_that_names_no_file_a_dataset_comes_from_is_a_word_of_the_name checks that orders.west and orders.backup are NOT_FOUND with west and backup in absent_words and orders as the first candidate, and that orders.csv, orders.json and orders.parquet resolve to orders.

In a one-name reference with a word beyond stopwords and hint words, _score now keeps every Latin-script word, stopwords and hint words included. test_a_stopword_or_hint_word_inside_a_name_is_a_word_of_the_name checks that orders_file, data_orders, orders_latest and lib_latest are NOT_FOUND naming file, data or latest, with lib_loans, lib_members and lib_branch_hours as the nearest names for lib_latest, and that orders_imported still resolves because the dataset's description has imported.

The same test checks that latest and 'the latest lib table' resolve as before. A before-and-after comparison of latest, yesterday, the_latest, imported, yesterday's sales, latest sales and the CJK references 销售 and 最新 changed only sales_latest. The new tests fail on the PR head and pass with the change. README.md and the datasets.py module docstring state the rule, and the full pytest suite passes.

note: Scope is DatasetResolver._score in agent_backend/core/resolver/datasets.py. CJK words keep their scoring because only Latin-script stopwords and hint words are added back. Hints still apply their filters when a dataset accounts for the word.
